messages.subject: Re: Best seeds for my area
messages.text:
Hi Ann,

Good news for zone 9B, all of our milkweed species will do well in your area. A few are particularly well-suited to the Texas heat:

- Asclepias tuberosa (Butterfly milkweed): thrives in dry, sunny conditions and loves well-drained soil
- Asclepias incarnata (Swamp milkweed): more versatile, tolerates both dry and wetter soils
- Asclepias syriaca (Common milkweed): very vigorous and easy to establish

For a warm climate like yours, you can plant in spring once temperatures are consistently warm. When sowing directly in the ground in fall, or into soil that is already warm, no cold stratification is needed.

You can browse all available species here: https://lasclay.com/en/products/milkweed-seeds

Sorry for the long wait on this one, things have been very intense on our end and your message deserved a reply much sooner. Happy to point you to the right species if you'd like help narrowing it down.

Warmly,
__
 Gabriel Gouveia 
Co-founder
Lasclay.com
